prompt:
A native macOS desktop app screen for ConceptStudio at 1536 by 1024, rendered edge to edge with crisp readable text, no device, desk or window shadow around it. The screen is ConceptStudio's Review step. ConceptStudio is a Mac app that turns a folder of photos into a trained image-model adapter; on Review the user checks each training caption beside its photo. Real content: project "NORA7 portrait", 24 samples, 19 marked final. The current sample is window.jpg, a woman in a burgundy knitted turtleneck standing beside a bright window. Its caption, editable: "NORA7, a person, wearing a burgundy knitted turtleneck, standing beside a window with her body turned to the side and face toward the camera. Warm light falls from the left; a bookshelf and plants are softly blurred in the background." NORA7 is the trigger word, the concept being learned; the caption describes everything except the concept. One sample needs attention: studio.jpg carries a reviewer note, "Describes the concept itself: remove curly dark hair." Actions by name: Save caption, Mark final, Re-caption, and Next: Publish. Frame: the window's sidebar lists nine steps in three groups, Prepare training data (Images, Concepts, Mapping), Write captions (Captioning, Review, Publish), Train your model (GPU pods, Training, Monitor), with Review selected; a small "Demo, no charges" status at the top right.
What leads: the current sample shown as one large instant print, the photograph above and a wide white bottom margin holding the trigger NORA7 set large, then the caption as an editable text field inside that margin; the other samples run as a strip of small prints with their state stamped on each margin (final, edited, needs attention), excluded prints visible but struck through.
Visual law: a film-back charcoal shell and sidebar around a warm instant-print white working area; photographs are never tinted; one grotesque typeface carries both the large trigger and the caption; a single developing-orange accent rings only the print under review and fills the primary action. No handwriting, no tilted prints, no scrapbook decoration: a calm, exact working tool.

Every sample thumbnail shows the same woman, the one concept being learned, in different settings and clothes; only the setting changes between samples.
